diagnostic_evidence.quote: where the inequality follows from the second condition in the definition of $\mc{R}_t$

issues.failure_explanation: The definition of the ridge only gives E(z)^T grad log p(z)=0 and eigenvalue bounds on the span of E(z). The proof needs these for n in N_z(R_t), the geometric normal space of the manifold R_t. The tangent space of the zero set of G(x)=E(x)^T grad log p(x) is ker(E^T H + (∇E)^T grad log p); since grad log p(z) has a nonzero tangential component and eigenvectors rotate (∇E≠0 unless the Hessian eigenvectors are constant, as in the two-point example), the tangent space differs from the top-d* eigenspace in general, so n need not lie in span E(z). Hence neither ⟨n,∇log p(z)⟩=0 nor ⟨n,H n⟩≤−β‖n‖² follows. The same identification (N = E) is used in Lemma second fundamental form bound and Lemma normal velocity field.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add and prove a quantitative alignment lemma bounding the angle between N_z(R_t) and span E(z) (in terms of ‖∇³log p‖·‖∇log p‖/eigengap) and carry the resulting extra term through the Itô estimate, or add an explicit alignment hypothesis.
issues.overall_effect: The core contraction inequality of the align stage and the curvature/velocity estimates of the ridge are unproven for data sets whose Hessian eigenframe varies along the ridge (any non-collinear configuration).
issues.title: Normal space of the ridge is silently identified with the bottom eigenspace E(z)
issues.why_classification: A contained new lemma (or added hypothesis) can restore the argument with an extra error term, but it is nontrivial and not present in the source.

issues.failure_explanation: D_{T-t} and Π_{T-t} are only defined inside the tube T_{T-t}(ρ_{T-t}). The SDE has non-degenerate noise, so after t_in the process can leave the tube (and the tube itself moves and shrinks as ρ_{T-t}→0). The Itô computation and Gronwall step are applied on [t_in,t] as if the process stays inside; no stopping time or exit-probability control is given, so E[D_{T-t}(Ỹ_t)] is not even well defined for the stated range.

failure_location.quote: Once the processes enter $\mc{T}_{T-t}(\rho_t)$, we can track the evolution of $D_{T-t}$ via It\^o's formula.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the result with a stopped process (exit time from the tube) and add an estimate of the exit probability, or extend D by a smooth cutoff outside the tube and track the cutoff error.
issues.overall_effect: The alignment bound holds at most up to the exit time from the tube; the stated unconditional bound on [t_in,T−δ] is unsupported.
issues.title: Normal contraction bound asserted for all t≥t_in without controlling exit from the tube
issues.why_classification: Requires a stopping-time/exit-probability argument not in the source, but the contraction mechanism and rates survive on the event of staying in the tube.

issues.failure_explanation: With Y_t=z+n, 2⟨n,Y_t⟩=2‖n‖²+2⟨n,z⟩; the position term ⟨n,z⟩ is not zero in general (z is a point, not a tangent vector) and is omitted. It is of order ρ‖z‖.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Bound the omitted term by 2ρ_{T-t}·sup_{z∈R_t}‖z‖ and absorb it into B_{s,t}(d,R).
issues.overall_effect: The differential inequality is missing an O(ρ_{T-t}R) drift term; the stated bound survives because B_{s,t} already contains a ρR term.
issues.title: Drift inner product drops the term ⟨n, Π(Y_t)⟩

issues.failure_explanation: The differential inequality uses Lemma application closeness, valid only while Ỹ_t∈B^{(i)}_{T-t}; the Gronwall integration from t_in to T−δ requires Ỹ_u∈B^{(i)} for the same i on the whole interval, whereas the paper itself states the process only enters a dominant region near the end. Moreover d/dt E[‖ũ‖²] under a pointwise random condition is not a well-defined object without stopping times. The initial term exp(−∫)E‖ũ_{t_in}‖² is also dropped.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Introduce the entry time τ_i into B^{(i)} and the exit time, prove the inequality for the stopped process, and restate the bound with integral from τ_i (adding the exponentially damped initial term).
issues.overall_effect: The stated sliding bound is not established as written; a correct version must start from the (random) entry time into B^{(i)} and restrict to trajectories remaining there.
issues.title: Tangent bound integrates from t_in although membership in B^{(i)} is only pointwise
issues.why_classification: Needs a stopping-time reformulation; the qualitative sliding conclusion and √δ rate survive but the stated quantifier/range changes.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma important estimate bounds ∇m and ∇³log p, not the time derivative of eigenvectors. At a center the Hessian is −I/h+Σ/h² with ‖Σ‖=O(θR²), so the gap between λ_{d*} and λ_{d*+1} is itself O(θ/h²); eigenvector-perturbation bounds then give ‖∂_tU‖≈‖∂_tΣ‖/gap, which is not O(θ) without a further argument on the relative decay of second-nearest-center contributions. The asserted estimate is a nontrivial missing step.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove a Davis–Kahan-type bound for the rotation rate of U_t^{(i)} using the explicit form of Σ(t,m_t^{(i)}) and a uniqueness/gap assumption on nearest neighbours, or replace U^{(i)} by a fixed frame.
issues.overall_effect: The O(d) size of ε̃^{(i)} in the tangent inequality, and hence the d√δ term, is unsupported as written.
issues.title: Unsupported O(θ) bound on the time derivative of the top-d* eigenprojection at centers
issues.why_classification: A contained eigenvector-perturbation lemma is required; the result is plausible but not established.

issues.failure_explanation: The iteration factor is (1−2ηλ_j)^k, which decays iff 0<η<1/λ_1. For η∈[1/λ_1,2/λ_1) the top mode has |1−2ηλ_1|≥1, so Err_train(k) does not decay and A_k does not converge to A_∞, contradicting the stated consequences and the appendix's own stability condition.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the hypothesis by η<1/λ_1 in both statements.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem and Proposition are false for η∈[1/λ_1,2/λ_1); the geometric-decay conclusion needs η<1/λ_1.

issues.why_classification: Single hypothesis correction, consistent with the appendix, preserving all conclusions.

issues.failure_explanation: The equation (I−S)τ = P^∥(∇v)^T n involves ⟨n,∇_{E_i}v⟩, i.e. the normal component of the derivative of the normal field v along tangent directions (‖P^⊥∇v P^∥‖). W_t is defined as the tangential component ‖P^∥∇v P^∥‖, and Prop constant estimation bounds only that tangential component via ∇P^⊥. For a hypersurface with v=φ n̂, the needed quantity is |∇_uφ| (variation of normal speed), which is unrelated to W_t. Hence ‖τ_t‖≤ρW_t/(1−ρ/r) is not proved.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine the constant as sup‖P^⊥(∇v_t u)‖ over unit tangent u and prove a data-dependent bound for it (derivatives of ∂_t∇log p_t along the ridge), then propagate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $\mc{R}_t$ is a (piecewise) $C^2$-embedded submanifold in $\mb{R}^d$ with a reach no smaller than $r_t>0$

issues.failure_explanation: Federer's reach satisfies reach ≤ 1/(max curvature); a curvature bound gives an upper, not a lower, bound on the reach. The reach can be arbitrarily small due to global bottlenecks (distinct ridge branches approaching each other) or corners, which are exactly the situations described by 'piecewise' ridges (e.g. the letter-M or three-point examples). Hence positive reach and its rate are not established from the second-fundamental-form bound.

issues.overall_effect: The claimed verification that Assumption ridge set holds under Assumption data, with explicit r_t, is unsupported; positive reach must be assumed or proved by a global argument.
issues.title: Reach lower bound derived from a false inequality (reach ≥ 1/curvature)
issues.why_classification: The framework can retreat to Assumption ridge set as a hypothesis, but the advertised data-dependent verification requires a new global argument.

issues.failure_explanation: The ridge R_t is a deterministic set that passes through regions where no center dominates (e.g. the bisector point x_1=0 of the two-point ridge, where the softmax weights are 1/2,1/2 for every t). The closure of ∪B^{(i)} never contains such points, so the 'with probability 1' argument does not bound sup_{z∈R_t}‖∇³log p_t(z)‖ by the θ_t-small dominant-region bound; near the bisector ‖∇³log p_t‖=Θ(R³/h_t³). The same misapplication underlies Lemma key estimation. Consequently r_t=Ω(h_t²θ_t^{-1}R^{-3}) with θ_t^{-1}=exp(o(1/h_t)) (reach growing to infinity) is unfounded; the supportable bound is only Ω(h_t²R^{-3}). Stage 1's proof needs ρ_δ²≳d h_δ (impossible with ρ_δ≍h_δ²), while Stage 2's remainder needs ρ_t≲β_t h_t³R^{-3}; no single choice of ρ_t reconciles them once the inflated reach is removed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must bound ∇³log p_t and ∂_t m on the whole ridge (including inter-center regions), derive an honest r_t, and re-prove the reach stage with a tube radius compatible with both Stage 1 (ρ_δ²≳dh_δ) and Stage 2 (ρ_t≲β_t h_t³/R³) or under an additional explicit reach hypothesis.
issues.overall_effect: The data-dependent reach/velocity rates, the reach-stage theorem (which requires a tube wide enough to capture Gaussian noise of size √(dh_δ)), and the B-term/ρ choice in the align stage are unsupported as written.
issues.title: Third-derivative and velocity bounds valid only on center-dominant regions are applied on the whole ridge
issues.why_classification: The advertised verification under Assumption data alone collapses, and the reach-stage theorem as stated loses its proof; reconciling the stages needs a new argument.
